mainTopic: How אביי and רבא read the ברייתא about a slave's tooth and eye, and whether it proves that הכחשה תחילת הזמה היא.
overview: The גמרא is working through a ברייתא about witnesses who say a master injured both the tooth and the eye of his עבד כנעני. Either injury frees the slave, so the order matters: the second injury was done to a free man, and the master must pay for it. First the גמרא explains אביי's reading. In the סיפא, a second set of witnesses agrees the injuries happened but reverses their order and also makes the first set זוממין. It must date the injuries earlier, and the master must already have stood trial, or else the זוממין would owe the whole slave. Then רב אחא asks רב אשי where רבא's proof that הכחשה תחילת הזמה comes from, since in the רישא the middle witnesses were never really contradicted. רב אשי answers that רבא reads the סיפא as a three-set case: a first pair is contradicted, then made זוממין, and still pays, which proves רבא's rule. אביי replies that only the רישא needs three sets, because a slave is happy with any testimony that frees him. Finally רבי זירא starts a new challenge to the ברייתא's basic rule, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The ending of the ברייתא shows what its beginning is about
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא states its proof: the סיפא deals with מיפך והזמה, so the רישא must deal with the same kind of case.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since the last part of the ברייתא is a case of reversing the order and making the witnesses זוממין, the first part is also a case of reversing the order and making them זוממין.
steps.whatsHappening: Continuing אביי's reading of the ברייתא, the גמרא announces a proof about the first case based on the last case. The next steps will show why the last case must be מיפך והזמה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea is that the two halves of a ברייתא are built in parallel. If we can show that the סיפא is about witnesses who switched the order of the injuries and were caught as זוממין, the רישא must be about the same setup. This step only states the claim. The proof itself comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: The last part of a משנה or ברייתא
The first part of a משנה or ברייתא
Reversing: the second set of witnesses says the order of events was the opposite
Making witnesses זוממין: proving they could not have seen what they claimed

phrases.english: From the fact that the latter clause is about reversal and הזמה,
phrases.notes: Reversal here means the second witnesses say the injuries happened in the opposite order.

phrases.english: the first clause is also about reversal and הזמה.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִדְּסֵיפָא בְּמֵיפַךְ וַהֲזַמָּה, רֵישָׁא נָמֵי בְּמֵיפַךְ וַהֲזַמָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues אביי's reading of the ברייתא from the previous amud (two sets of witnesses, מיפך והזמה) by offering a proof from the סיפא about how to read the רישא.
steps.raayaObject: That the רישא of the ברייתא deals with witnesses who are both reversed and made זוממין.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The parallel structure with the סיפא of the same ברייתא.

steps.title: Quoting the ending of the ברייתא: tooth first, then eye
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the סיפא: witnesses say the master knocked out the tooth and then blinded the eye, and when they are found זוממין they pay the master the value of an eye.
steps.simpleTranslation: As the last part teaches: 'We testify that so-and-so knocked out his slave's tooth and then blinded his eye.' This is what the slave claims. If these witnesses are then found to be זוממין, they pay the master the value of an eye.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the סיפא of the ברייתא word for word, so it can examine it in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the tooth came first, the slave went free right then, so the eye was blinded on a free man and the master owes him the value of the eye. That is why this testimony helps the slave. If the witnesses turn out to be זוממין, they must pay the master the eye value they tried to make him lose.

keyTerms.meaning: Tooth and eye: either injury by a master frees his עבד כנעני
Witnesses proven false, who must pay what they tried to cause
The value of an eye
Here it means the master of the slave, not a rabbi

steps.confusionAlert: Here רב means the slave's master, not a rabbi or teacher.

phrases.english: As the latter clause teaches:
'We testify about so-and-so
that he knocked out his slave's tooth,
and then blinded his eye'
— for that is what the slave says;
phrases.notes: This order helps the slave: he went free from the tooth, so the master owes him for the eye.

phrases.english: and they were found to be זוממין —
they pay the value of an eye to the master.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the text of the סיפא that step 1 relies on.
steps.raayaObject: That the סיפא is a case of מיפך והזמה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ruling of the סיפא that the זוממין pay only the value of an eye.

steps.title: What is the case? It cannot be that the injuries are denied completely
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what situation the סיפא describes, and rules out the case where the second witnesses deny any injury, because then the זוממין would owe the value of the whole slave.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case? If the later witnesses do not agree that there was any injury at all, then the false witnesses should have to pay the master the value of the whole slave!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what exact case the סיפא is talking about, and immediately rejects one possible answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the second set says nothing happened at all, the first witnesses tried to take away the entire slave from the master by setting him free. Then their payment as זוממין should be the full value of the slave. Since the ברייתא says they pay only the value of an eye, this cannot be the case.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? What situation are we talking about?
The later ones: the second set of witnesses
Injury
To pay

phrases.english: What are the circumstances?

phrases.aramaic: אִי דְּלָא קָא מוֹדוּ לְהוּ בָּתְרָאֵי
phrases.english: If the later witnesses do not agree with them
about the injury at all,
the value of the entire slave to the master
they should have to pay him!
phrases.notes: Without any injury, the slave would not go free at all, so the false witnesses tried to make the master lose the whole slave.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֵיכִי דָמֵי? אִי דְּלָא קָא מוֹדוּ לְהוּ בָּתְרָאֵי בְּחַבְלָא כְּלָל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Examines the סיפא quoted in step 2 to figure out its exact case.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What case the סיפא describes, so it can be shown to be מיפך והזמה.

steps.title: So everyone agrees the injuries happened
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that both sets of witnesses must agree that the master caused the injuries. The disagreement is only about something else, which the גמרא will spell out next.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is obvious that all of them agree about the injury,
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the only remaining possibility: both sets of witnesses agree the master injured the slave. The sentence finishes in step 5, which shows the dispute is only about the order of the injuries.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the payment is only the value of an eye, the second witnesses cannot be denying the injuries. So both sets agree the tooth and eye were injured, and the slave goes free either way. This sets up the point that the second witnesses only reversed the order, which is מיפך together with הזמה.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, it is obvious: the only option left
They agree, they admit
All of them: both sets of witnesses

steps.whatToRemember: The זוממין pay only the value of an eye, not the whole slave. That shows both sets of witnesses agree the injuries happened, so the only dispute can be about their order.

phrases.english: Rather, it is obvious —
that all of them agree about the injury,

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא פְּשִׁיטָא דְּקָא מוֹדוּ כּוּלְּהוּ בְּחַבְלָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 3 by taking the only option left after the first one was rejected.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Both sets of witnesses agree that the master caused the injuries. The dispute must be only about their order, which will be spelled out next.

steps.title: The second witnesses reversed the order and made the first witnesses זוממין
steps.stepSummary: The disagreement is that the second witnesses reversed the order of the injuries, and in the same testimony they made the first witnesses זוממין.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the second witnesses reversed the order of events, and they made the first witnesses זוממין.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the answer from step 4. The two sets of witnesses disagree only about the order of the injuries, and the second set also proves the first set false through הזמה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sets agree the master hurt the slave, so the slave's freedom itself is not in question. The second witnesses say the eye came first and the tooth second. This changes what the master owes, and that is why the זוממין pay only the value of an eye.

keyTerms.meaning: They reversed it, meaning they swapped the order of the events.
They made them זוממין, by showing the first witnesses were not there.
Reversal: the second witnesses tell the same events in the opposite order.

steps.whatToRemember: In the סיפא, both sets of witnesses agree the master caused the injuries. The second set reverses the order and also makes the first set זוממין.

phrases.english: And they reversed it
phrases.notes: The printed גמרא has the words in round brackets; the corrected wording, in square brackets, says the second witnesses reversed the order.

phrases.english: and made them זוממין.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the answer begun in step 4 by stating exactly what the witnesses disagree about.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The second witnesses agree the master caused the injuries, but they reverse the order and also make the first witnesses זוממין.

steps.title: When did the injuries happen? The later-date option fails
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what timing the second witnesses gave. It rejects the possibility that they placed the injuries later, because then the זוממין would owe the whole slave.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case? If the second witnesses placed the events at a later time, the false witnesses should still pay the master the value of the whole slave. When they tried to make the master liable, he was not yet liable for anything.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks when, according to the second witnesses, the injuries really happened. It rules out the idea that they happened later than the first witnesses said.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the injuries came later, then on the date the first witnesses gave, the master owed nothing at all. Their false testimony would have taken a whole slave from him, so as זוממין they should pay the full slave value. That contradicts the ברייתא, which says they pay only the value of an eye.

keyTerms.meaning: They moved the date later than the first witnesses said.
The latter ones, meaning the second set of witnesses.
Still, or not yet.
Someone who is subject to a liability.

phrases.english: And what are the circumstances?

phrases.aramaic: אִי דְּקָא מְאַחֲרִי אַחוֹרֵי הָנֵי בָּתְרָאֵי –
phrases.english: If these latter witnesses moved the date later,

phrases.aramaic: אַכַּתִּי דְּמֵי עֶבֶד לְרַב בָּעֵי שַׁלּוֹמֵי;
phrases.english: they still need to pay the master the value of a slave;
phrases.notes: He means the value of the whole slave, not just the value of an eye.

phrases.english: for when they were making the man liable,

phrases.aramaic: אַכַּתִּי גַּבְרָא לָאו בַּר חִיּוּבָא הוּא!
phrases.english: the man was still not subject to liability!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהֵיכִי דָמֵי? אִי דְּקָא מְאַחֲרִי אַחוֹרֵי הָנֵי בָּתְרָאֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Now that the case is reversal plus הזמה, the גמרא asks what timing the second witnesses gave.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Did the second witnesses date the injuries later or earlier than the first witnesses?
steps.kashyaTarget: The option that the second witnesses dated the injuries later.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: On the first witnesses' date the master owed nothing, so the זוממין would owe the whole slave and not just an eye.

steps.title: The second witnesses must have placed the injuries earlier
steps.stepSummary: Since the later date does not work, the second witnesses must have placed the injuries at an earlier date.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the second witnesses placed the events at an earlier time.
steps.whatsHappening: Having ruled out the later date, the גמרא concludes that the second witnesses said the injuries happened earlier than the first witnesses claimed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the injuries came earlier, then by the first witnesses' date the master was already responsible for the injuries. So the false testimony only changed the details, the order of eye and tooth, and not the whole liability.

keyTerms.meaning: They moved the date earlier than the first witnesses said.
Rather. It introduces the remaining option after one was rejected.

phrases.english: Rather, it must be that they moved the date earlier,
these latter witnesses.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא דְּקָא מְקַדְּמִי קַדּוֹמֵי הָנֵי בָּתְרָאֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the only option left after step 6 rejected the later date.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The second witnesses dated the injuries earlier than the first witnesses did.

steps.title: If the master had not yet stood trial, the full slave would still be owed
steps.stepSummary: Even with an earlier date, if the master had not yet been judged in court, the זוממין would still owe the whole slave, because the master was not yet liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if the master had not yet stood trial, the false witnesses should still pay him the value of the whole slave, since the man was not yet liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא narrows the case further by ruling out one more possibility. This sets up the next move, where the גמרא will say the master had already been judged.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An earlier date alone is not enough. If no court had yet ruled the master liable, then at the time of the first testimony he was not yet obligated, and the זוממין would again owe the full slave. So the case must involve a master who had already stood trial.

keyTerms.meaning: Stood trial, meaning he was judged and ruled liable in בית דין.
Is liable or obligated.
All of it, the whole.

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the earlier date alone solves the case. The גמרא shows that the master must also have already been judged in court, or the זוממין would owe the whole slave.

phrases.english: And if he had not stood trial,
phrases.notes: He means the master had not yet been brought to בית דין and ruled liable for the injuries.

phrases.english: they would still need the value of the whole slave
to pay to the master,
since the man was not yet liable!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the earlier-date answer of step 7 by rejecting the case where the master had not yet been judged.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The case where the master had not yet stood trial at the time of the first testimony.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The master would not yet be liable, so the זוממין would owe the whole slave, against the ברייתא, which says they pay only an eye.

steps.title: The master had already stood trial
steps.stepSummary: After rejecting the later date (step 6) and the case where the master had not yet stood trial (step 8), the גמרא concludes that the second witnesses gave an earlier date and that the master had already been judged in court.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is a case where the master already stood trial.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its final picture of the case. The master had already been judged in court for these injuries.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 8 showed a problem: if the master had not yet been judged, the זוממין would owe the whole slave. Here the master had already been judged, so he was already liable. That avoids the problem.

keyTerms.meaning: stood trial; was already judged in court
rather; introduces the corrected answer

steps.whatToRemember: In אביי's reading, the case of the סיפא is now fully defined. The second witnesses reverse the order and make the first set זוממין, and the master had already stood trial. So the witnesses' lie does not cost the whole slave. רבא reads the ברייתא differently, as the next steps show.

phrases.english: Rather, it is where he had already stood trial.
phrases.notes: "He" is the master. The court had already ruled on him for these injuries.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the problem raised in Step 8 by adding the detail that the master was already judged.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The case is one where the master had already stood trial, so he was already liable before the false testimony.

steps.title: Where did רבא learn his rule from?
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בריה דרב איקא asks רב אשי which part of the ברייתא רבא used. He argues that the רישא cannot be the source, because the middle witnesses there were not contradicted.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא son of רב איקא said to רב אשי: Where does רבא's inference come from? If you say from the first part, then in the first part, are the middle witnesses contradicted?
steps.whatsHappening: A new challenge opens. רב אחא asks which case in the ברייתא proves רבא's rule, and he starts by attacking the first case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא's rule depends on witnesses who were first contradicted and then made זוממין. רב אחא asks whether the middle set in the רישא was ever really contradicted. If they were not, the רישא proves nothing for רבא.

keyTerms.meaning: a precise inference drawn from the wording of a source
the first part of a ברייתא or משנה
are contradicted (their testimony is rejected by other witnesses)
the middle set of witnesses

steps.confusionAlert: Here רבא reads the case as involving three sets of witnesses: first, middle, and last. The "middle ones" are the second set, who reversed the order of the injuries.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִיקָא לְרַב אָשֵׁי:
phrases.english: Rav Aḥa, son of Rav Ika, said to Rav Ashi:
Rava's inference, from where is it?
phrases.notes: רבא used this ברייתא to prove that contradicting witnesses is the first step toward making them זוממין.

phrases.english: If you say it is from the first clause,
in the first clause, are the middle witnesses contradicted?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from אביי's two-set reading of the ברייתא (steps 1–9) to רבא's opposing proof, which reads the ברייתא as a three-set case. רב אחא asks which clause רבא's proof comes from.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's proof from the רישא of the ברייתא that הכחשה is the beginning of הזמה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A proof needs witnesses who were contradicted and then made זוממין. In the רישא the middle witnesses were never really contradicted.

steps.title: The middle witnesses would have been believed
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא explains that without the הזמה, the court would have ruled like the middle witnesses, because יש בכלל מאתים מנה. So it is the first witnesses who are contradicted, not the middle ones.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since if they had not been made זוממין, the testimony would stand like them, because we would rule like them, since a hundred is included in two hundred. Therefore it is the first witnesses who are contradicted, and the middle ones are not contradicted at all.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא finishes his challenge. He proves that the middle witnesses in the רישא were not contradicted, so the רישא cannot be רבא's source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The middle witnesses claimed the master owes the smaller amount. The first witnesses claimed a bigger amount, and a bigger claim already includes the smaller one. So both groups agree on the smaller amount, and the court would follow the middle witnesses. Only the first group's extra claim is pushed aside, so the first group is the one that is contradicted.

keyTerms.meaning: are made עדים זוממין
testimony
a hundred is included in two hundred; testimony to a large sum includes the smaller sum
the first set of witnesses
therefore

steps.whatToRemember: In the רישא, the middle witnesses' testimony would have been fully accepted. So they were never "contradicted" before being made זוממין, and the רישא cannot prove רבא's rule.
steps.whyThisMatters: This forces the גמרא to look elsewhere in the ברייתא for רבא's source, or to rethink his proof.

phrases.english: Since if they had not been made זוממין,
the testimony would stand in accordance with them,
as we would decide the judgment in accordance with them,
since a hundred is included within two hundred;
therefore it is the first ones who are contradicted,
the middle ones are not contradicted at all!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains and completes the challenge raised in Step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the middle witnesses in the רישא were contradicted before being made זוממין
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Because יש בכלל מאתים מנה, the court would accept the middle witnesses' smaller amount. Only the first witnesses' extra claim is rejected, so the middle witnesses were never contradicted.

steps.title: רבא learned from the סיפא, not the רישא
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי answers that רבא read the סיפא as a three-set case too, and drew his proof from the סיפא.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: רבא holds that since the רישא has three sets of witnesses, the סיפא also has three, and he draws his proof from the סיפא.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי answers רב אחא's question from Step 10. He says רבא never used the רישא. He used the סיפא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אחא showed that the רישא cannot prove רבא's rule. רב אשי agrees, but he moves the proof to the סיפא. The סיפא only mentions one pair of witnesses. רבא reasons that the רישא has three sets, so the סיפא must also have three, and that makes the proof possible.

keyTerms.meaning: The first clause of a משנה or ברייתא
The latter clause of a משנה or ברייתא
Sets or groups of witnesses
He infers or derives a precise point from the text

phrases.english: He said to him: Rava holds:
phrases.notes: This is רב אשי answering רב אחא בריה דרב איקא.

phrases.english: Since the first clause deals with three sets of witnesses,
the latter clause also deals with three;
and he infers it from the latter clause.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ, רָבָא סָבַר: מִדְּרֵישָׁא בְּשָׁלֹשׁ כִּיתּוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב אחא's challenge by moving רבא's source from the רישא to the סיפא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Relocating the source: the proof comes from a different clause, read the same way as the רישא.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבא's proof came from the רישא, where the middle witnesses were never really contradicted.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבא's proof comes from the סיפא, which he reads as a three-set case too.

steps.title: Defining the three-set case in the סיפא
steps.stepSummary: The סיפא is explained: a first pair testifies tooth-then-eye and the court rules. A second pair contradicts them by saying eye-then-tooth. Then the first pair is made into זוממין and pays the master the value of an eye.
steps.simpleTranslation: For example, two witnesses came and said the master knocked out the slave's tooth and then blinded his eye, and the court ruled based on them. Then two other witnesses came and said he blinded the eye and then knocked out the tooth, contradicting the first pair. Then the first pair were found to be זוממין, and they pay the value of an eye to the master.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא spells out exactly what case רבא sees in the סיפא. This sets up the proof that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The order of the injuries matters. If the tooth came first, the slave goes free because of the tooth, and the master owes him for the eye. If the eye came first, the master owes only for the tooth. The second pair contradicts the first pair before the first pair is made into זוממין. Even so, the ברייתא says the first pair pays the master.

keyTerms.meaning: The court ruled the judgment
They contradict, saying the facts happened differently
Conspiring witnesses, shown to have been elsewhere at the time
The value of an eye

steps.confusionAlert: The 'other two' witnesses do not appear in the ברייתא. רבא adds them because he assumes the סיפא, like the רישא, has three sets of witnesses.

phrases.english: For example, where two came and said:
"He knocked out his tooth and blinded his eye,"
and the court ruled the case based on their word;
and two other witnesses came and said:
"He blinded his eye and knocked out his tooth,"
so they contradict those first witnesses;
and then the first ones were found to be conspiring witnesses —
they pay the value of an eye to the master.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Fills in the three-set case that Step 12 said is in the סיפא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Case definition that supports the answer of Step 12.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The סיפא seemed to have only one pair of witnesses.
steps.terutzMaskana: The סיפא has a first pair that is contradicted, and then made into זוממין, and they still pay.

steps.title: Why would contradicted witnesses pay?
steps.stepSummary: If a contradiction did not count as the start of הזמה, the first pair should be exempt, since they were already contradicted before the הזמה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you think a contradiction is not the start of הזמה, why do they pay? They were already contradicted from the start!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now draws רבא's proof out of the case. It asks why the first pair would pay if contradicted witnesses could not later become זוממין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first pair was contradicted before they were made into זוממין. If a contradiction cancelled their testimony for the purposes of הזמה, they would escape payment. The ברייתא says they pay, so the opposite view cannot be right.

keyTerms.meaning: A contradiction, when other witnesses dispute the facts
The beginning of the הזמה process
From the outset, from the beginning

phrases.english: And if it enters your mind
that a contradiction is not the start of הזמה,
why do they pay?
They were already contradicted from the outset!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי סָלְקָא דַעְתָּךְ הַכְחָשָׁה לָאו תְּחִילַּת הֲזָמָה הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the case set up in Step 13 to build the proof.
steps.raayaObject: That הכחשה is the beginning of הזמה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The סיפא of the ברייתא, where witnesses who were contradicted and then made into זוממין still pay.

steps.title: Contradiction is the start of הזמה
steps.stepSummary: Conclusion: הכחשה תחילת הזמה היא. Witnesses who were contradicted can still later be punished as זוממין.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, learn from this: a contradiction is the start of הזמה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes רבא's proof. A contradiction does not stop the witnesses from being made into זוממין later.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא's ruling only makes sense if a contradiction is the first stage of הזמה. So רבא's rule is supported by the סיפא, and רב אחא's challenge is answered.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from it, a formula for drawing a conclusion

steps.whatToRemember: רבא's proof that הכחשה תחילת הזמה היא comes from the סיפא, read as a three-set case. The first pair was contradicted, then made into זוממין, and they still pay.
steps.whyThisMatters: This rule decides whether witnesses who were already contradicted by other witnesses can still be punished as עדים זוממין.

phrases.english: Rather, learn from it:
a contradiction is the start of הזמה.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ, הַכְחָשָׁה תְּחִילַּת הֲזָמָה הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: States the conclusion that the reasoning of Step 14 forces.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: הכחשה תחילת הזמה היא: witnesses who were contradicted can later be made into זוממין and must pay.

steps.title: אביי agrees the רישא needs three sets of witnesses
steps.stepSummary: אביי grants that the רישא must involve three sets of witnesses, because the ברייתא says 'the master says so.'
steps.simpleTranslation: And אביי would answer you: Granted, the first case cannot be explained without three sets of witnesses, because it teaches 'as the master says so.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins showing how אביי would push back against רבא's proof. First, אביי admits one point: the רישא really does need three sets of witnesses.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the רישא, the testimony is described as good for the master. That only makes sense if an earlier, worse testimony against the master had come first and was then knocked down. So אביי agrees that three sets are forced in the רישא, and he will draw the difference with the סיפא next.

keyTerms.meaning: Granted / it makes sense (concedes one side before pointing to a problem)
The first part of the ברייתא (the case where the master benefits)
It is impossible without; it must be
Sets (groups) of witnesses

phrases.english: And Abaye would say to you:
Granted, the first clause —
it cannot be without three sets of witnesses,
since it teaches "as the master says so";

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens אביי's rebuttal to רבא's proof from the סיפא by first granting the point about the רישא.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Partial. This line only grants the רישא; the actual rejection of the proof comes in the next step.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Sets up the claim that the reasoning which forces three sets in the רישא does not carry over to the סיפא.

steps.title: The סיפא does not need three sets of witnesses
steps.stepSummary: 'The slave says so' proves nothing in the סיפא, because a slave is happy with any testimony that frees him. So the סיפא can be a two-set case, and רבא's proof falls away.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the last case — why do I need three sets of witnesses? Because it says 'as the slave says so'? A slave will say anything, since he is happy to go free.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי rejects רבא's proof from the סיפא. The words 'the slave says so' do not force a third set of witnesses.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the רישא, 'the master says so' points to an earlier testimony that was worse for him. A slave, though, goes free under either order of the injuries, so any testimony pleases him. 'The slave says so' therefore does not show there was an earlier, worse testimony. The סיפא can be a simple two-set case, and then it gives no proof that הכחשה תחילת הזמה היא.

keyTerms.meaning: The last part of the ברייתא (the case where the slave benefits)
Anything at all; whatever
It is pleasing / good for him
Freedom (a slave going free)

steps.whatToRemember: According to אביי, only the רישא is forced to be a three-set case. The סיפא can be a two-set case, so רבא's proof that הכחשה תחילת הזמה היא does not hold for אביי.

phrases.english: But the latter clause —
why do I need three sets of witnesses?
Because "as the slave says so"?!
A slave would say anything,
since he is pleased to go out to freedom.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא סֵיפָא לְמָה לִי שָׁלֹשׁ כִּיתּוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes אביי's rebuttal by showing that the reason for three sets in the רישא does not apply to the סיפא.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects רבא's proof from the סיפא (steps 12–15) as binding on אביי.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed the סיפא must be a three-set case. But 'the slave says so' does not force that, since a slave gains freedom under either testimony.

steps.title: רבי זירא begins a new challenge to the ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא starts a new objection against the ברייתא's basic assumption about a master who injures his slave twice, beginning with 'say: he blinded his eye.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא objected: Say instead: he blinded his eye —
steps.whatsHappening: A new challenge begins here. רבי זירא starts to question the basic assumption of the ברייתא, and his full point continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the debate was about how many sets of witnesses are in the case. רבי זירא now targets the underlying assumption itself: that when a master causes two injuries, he must pay the slave for the second one. He starts building an alternative reading ('say: he blinded his eye'), and the rest of the argument comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: Challenged it / raised a strong objection against it
Say instead (offering a different way to see the case)
Blinded

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira objects to it,
say: if he blinded his eye —

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves away from the הכחשה/הזמה debate to challenge the ברייתא's underlying rule about payment for a second injury.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's assumption that a master who injures his slave twice must pay for the second injury.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי זירא proposes another way to see the case, starting with the blinding of the eye. The full logic of the attack continues on the next amud.
